components.css: .ds-nav-sample { overflow: hidden; border: 1px solid #e2e8f0; border-radius: 16px; background: #f8fafc; font-family: var(--font-be-vietnam-pro), system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-utility { display: flex; min-height: 32px; align-items: center; gap: 8px; background: #020617; color: #cbd5e1; padding: 0 14px; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 600; } .ds-utility a { margin-left: auto; color: #93c5fd; text-decoration: none; } .ds-dot { width: 8px; height: 8px; border-radius: 9999px; background: #34d399; } .ds-nav { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; background: rgb(255 255 255 / .95); padding: 12px 14px; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px 0 rgb(15 23 42 / .05); } .ds-nav strong { color: #0f172a; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 900; letter-spacing: -.025em; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-links { display: flex; gap: 2px; margin-left: auto; } .ds-links a { border-radius: 8px; color: #475569; padding: 6px 8px; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 600; text-decoration: none; } .ds-links a:hover, .ds-links .ds-active { background: #eff6ff; color: #1d4ed8; } .ds-worker-quiet, .ds-nav-primary { border-radius: 8px; padding: 7px 10px; font: 700 11px/1.25 var(--font-be-vietnam-pro), system-ui, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; } .ds-worker-quiet { border: 1px solid #fed7aa; background: #fff7ed; color: #c2410c; } .ds-nav-primary { border: 0; background: #1d4ed8; color: #ffffff; } .ds-worker-quiet:focus-visible, .ds-nav-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #1d4ed8; outline-offset: 2px; } @media (max-width: 620px) { .ds-links { display: none; } .ds-worker-quiet { margin-left: auto; } }

components.css: .ds-choice { overflow: hidden; border-radius: 16px; background: #020617; color: #ffffff; font-family: var(--font-be-vietnam-pro), system-ui, sans-serif; box-shadow: 0 24px 60px -28px rgba(15, 23, 42, .65); } .ds-choice header { border-bottom: 1px solid #1e293b; padding: 20px; } .ds-choice h3 { margin: 0; font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.35; } .ds-choice p { margin: 4px 0 0; color: #cbd5e1; font-size: 13px; line-height: 1.5; } .ds-choice-row { display: grid; grid-template-columns: auto 1fr auto; gap: 12px; align-items: center; border-bottom: 1px solid #1e293b; padding: 16px 20px; } .ds-choice-row strong { font-size: 14px; } .ds-choice-row button { min-height: 36px; border: 0; border-radius: 10px; background: #1d4ed8; color: #ffffff; padding: 8px 10px; font: 700 12px/1.25 var(--font-be-vietnam-pro), system-ui, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; } .ds-choice-row:last-child button { background: #ea580c; } .ds-choice-row button:hover { filter: brightness(1.08); } .ds-choice-row button:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #93c5fd; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-blue-icon, .ds-orange-icon { display: grid; width: 32px; height: 32px; place-items: center; border-radius: 10px; background: rgb(59 130 246 / .15); color: #93c5fd; } .ds-orange-icon { background: rgb(249 115 22 / .15); color: #fb923c; } @media (max-width: 420px) { .ds-choice-row { grid-template-columns: auto 1fr; } .ds-choice-row button { grid-column: 2; justify-self: start; } }

narrative.overview: The incumbent public experience pairs a bright slate information canvas with dark navy decision areas. It keeps workforce-related information direct and readable, using compact cards, durable labels, small Lucide icons, and clear state changes rather than ornamental treatments. Blue directs navigation, enterprise actions, focused fields, and information routing. Orange is a deliberate worker-facing counter-signal, used for job-seeking actions and their parallel navigation route.
keyCharacteristics: Light slate canvas and white work surfaces, separated by subtle borders or rings.
Navy bands and panels for high-attention orientation, choices, and results.
Blue for primary action, focus, information routing, and procedural progress.
Orange reserved for worker-oriented calls to action and supporting details.
Compact rounded containers, bold Vietnamese hierarchy, and responsive task-first layouts.

rules.name: The Signal-Lane Rule
rules.body: Use blue for enterprise and operational movement; reserve orange for worker-facing movement.

rules.name: The Contrast-First Rule
rules.body: Navy sections use white or pale-blue text; light sections use deep navy and slate text. State meaning must remain understandable from its label, icon, and placement—not color alone.

rules.name: The One-Family Rule
rules.body: Keep Be Vietnam Pro across public and operational surfaces. Hierarchy comes from weight, size, spacing, and color—not a decorative display face.

rules.name: The Border-Before-Shadow Rule
rules.body: On light surfaces, begin with the established slate border or ring. Add shadow only when a container must separate from its context or layer above it.

dos: Do keep the public canvas light slate and use white cards with the incumbent slate separation treatment.
Do use navy to group high-attention choices, orientation, and result summaries.
Do use blue for primary operational actions, focus states, navigation, and progress markers.
Do use orange specifically to differentiate worker-facing actions.
Do preserve clear labels, icon support, touch-friendly minimum control height, keyboard focus, and the reduced-motion fallback.
donts: Don't use orange as a competing generic primary accent on enterprise or operational flows.
Don't rely on color by itself for form errors, public-status cues, route identity, or progress.
Don't replace the restrained slate borders and controlled shadows with heavy gradients, glass effects, or decorative visual noise.
